{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:

let
  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;

  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # `orca-ide open` (orcaCli below) spawns the GUI detached, but every
    # wrapper layer execs the next, so this bwrap is the CLI's own child, and
    # --die-with-parent SIGKILLs the window the moment `open` returns. The
    # cost: bwrap forwards no signals, so when `orca-ide serve` is stopped by
    # a signal to the CLI (not Ctrl-C, which reaches the whole group, nor a
    # systemd cgroup stop), its Electron server outlives the bwrap it was
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher's bin/orca moves aside
    # to .orca-ide-unwrapped -- `orca` is orcaCli's name in the profile, and
    # tests/sandbox-fonts.sh finds the launcher by this one -- and
    # orca-ide-app execs it, the flag first when due.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      cat > $out/bin/orca-ide-app <<'EOF'
      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
      explicit=
      for a in "$@"; do
        case $a in --) break ;; --ozone-platform|--ozone-platform=*) explicit=1; break ;; esac
      done
      if [ -z "$explicit" ] && [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then
        set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"
      fi
      exec ${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped "$@"
      EOF
      chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide-app
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide-app'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide-app";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below;
  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
  # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
  # same reason parsec gets it.
  orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;

  # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
  # Linux) and `orca`. Upstream avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it is
  # usually the GNOME screen reader; it is not installed here, so `orca` is
  # the CLI too. (Were it installed, the profile comes first on PATH --
  # env.nix -- so `orca` would still be this CLI.) The skills say `orca-ide`.
  #
  # It is plain JavaScript: upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide runs it on the
  # bundled Electron in node mode, but nothing in it needs Electron, so it
  # runs on nixpkgs' node of the same major (Electron 43 bundles node 24)
  # with no sandbox -- a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's
  # own. Orca's own installer puts a shim dir on PATH only in Orca
  # terminals, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path that goes
  # stale on the next bump.
  #
  # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: the Orca binary for `orca-ide open` and `serve` to
  # launch; under plain node there is no other, and without it `open` fails
  # and `serve` refuses to start. NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as
  # ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS and cleared, as upstream's shim does.
  # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
  orcaCli = pkgs.runCommand "orca-cli-${version}" {
    pname = "orca-cli";
    inherit version;
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  } ''
    mkdir -p $out/bin
    cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
    #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
    export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE="''${ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app}"
    export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="''${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
    export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="''${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
    unset NODE_OPTIONS NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE
    exec ${pkgs.nodejs_24}/bin/node ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js "$@"
    EOF
    chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide
    ln -s orca-ide $out/bin/orca
  '';

  # Orca's agent skills, from the repo at the commit this AppImage was built
  # from: `orca skills install` pins `npx skills add` to it, and the bundled
  # resources/skills/current-manifest.json holds their sha256s. Bump this rev
  # with the version — it is the `sourceCommit` in out/main/index.js of
  # app.asar, and the test holds it to that. A fetch in this module rather
  # than a flake input, because the rev tracks `version` above, not the
  # repo's head; `nix flake update` does not touch it. The rev is in the
  # store name so a rev bump without a hash bump fails to fetch instead of
  # reusing the old tree. The skills are stubs that call
  # `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so they need orcaCli above.
  #
  # A subset of the bundled ten: no Jira, no emulator. Each is a read-only
  # store symlink, so Orca's own Settings > Skills "update" (npx skills add)
  # will fail on them or replace them, and home-manager then refuses to
  # clobber; update by bumping here instead.
  orcaSkillsSrc = pkgs.fetchFromGitHub rec {
    name = "orca-skills-${rev}";
    owner = "stablyai";
    repo = "orca";
    rev = "e6f7fba58e8e47b45e4343f99101b3ca9e05a5da";
    hash = "REDACTED";
  };
  orcaSkills = [
    "orca-cli" "orchestration" "computer-use" "orca-per-workspace-env"
    "orca-linear" "linear-tickets"
  ];

  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own

  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,

  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time

  # Chords Hyprland binds would be dead keys, so those actions are unbound --
  # on shiori 19 of them, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,

Both points from the CLI session are handled, and review round 4 is running on the merged HEAD (f2f78a6f). The `orca-cli-node` branch still isn't on master, so I merged it into this branch rather than wait.

**1. Signal to `orca-ide serve`:** case 6 in `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh`.
- It starts `serve` forced onto the Electron runtime, in an isolated session (Xvfb, its own D-Bus, throwaway HOME), sends SIGTERM to the CLI, and fails if any Electron process survives.
- Against the CLI branch's sandboxed GUI it fails: all 8 Electron processes were left running. Against this build it passes: all 7 went down with the CLI.
- By default `serve` runs on orcad, which is the pinned, unpatched node. Killing the CLI takes that down too, and it shows the pinned trees run unsandboxed.

**2. Rename and the CLI branch's tests:**
- The GUI is now `orca-ide-app`, and the build fails unless the desktop Exec is exactly `orca-ide-app %U`.
- The CLI branch's rule moved into my wrapper: no wayland flag when the caller passes `--ozone-platform` (as `serve` does with x11).
- `dieWithParent` is gone along with the sandbox.
- In `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`, the GUI argv check and the GUI-lifetime check (window outliving `orca-ide open`) are updated for the new wrapper.

On the merged tree: GUI tests 23/23, CLI tests 25/25, keybinding tests 32/32.

Round 3 also changed the fonts: Orca and everything it spawns now see your host's font config plus DejaVu. The old private config hid 627 of the host's font files from Orca's terminals.

**Still open:**
- Two clean review rounds in a row on this HEAD.
- If the CLI branch reaches master as different commits (rebased or squashed), I'll re-merge and review again.
- Your answer on nixGL: keep, drop, or strip the variables it passes into Orca's terminals.
- Then merge to master and run `hms`.

- `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh` passed 25/25.
- **Cleanup:** after my run, and after another session's run that overlapped it, the host had no `~/.cache/orca-gui-test.*` dirs, no `orca-gui-test*` units, and no leftover mounts. I checked from the host side through `systemd-run`.
  - The private D-Bus session does auto-start the host's `/usr/lib/xdg-document-portal` (a FUSE mount at `$T/run/doc`) and `gnome-keyring-daemon`. Both live only in the throwaway runtime dir and HOME, and both were gone once the unit stopped. That is isolated, just not the "no keyring at all" the comment suggests.
- **Generated wrapper:** it sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE`, runs the ozone check, then does a plain `exec …/lib/orca/orca-ide "$@"`. The desktop entry is `Exec=orca-ide-app %U`, and the `orca://` MimeType is kept.

## Critical
None.

## Important
**1. Merge left stale font claims, and `symbol-fonts.sh` checks the wrong font config.**
- `home.nix:175-177` says: "orca's sandbox DejaVu stays out on purpose … inside it fontconfig already ranks DejaVu ahead (measured: nothing moves)".
- `tests/symbol-fonts.sh:29` builds its throwaway config "over nixpkgs' conf.d (what orca.nix includes)" (code at around lines 170-176).
- Both came from orca-cli-node. After the merge there is no sandbox, and `orca.nix:184-198` includes the host's `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf`, not nixpkgs' conf.d. That "nothing moves" result was measured under the old config.
- **Failure scenario:** the symbol gap font does not yield to DejaVu, by design. If Arch's fontconfig ranks the gap font and DejaVu differently, some of the ~480 overlapping glyphs change face inside Orca. Because `FONTCONFIG_FILE` is now inherited, they also change in every terminal and agent Orca spawns.
- `symbol-fonts.sh` would still pass, because it tests nixpkgs' conf.d. `orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh` case 3 only checks five generic families and the list of font files, not per-glyph fallback.
- **Fix:** reword the comments, and point that `symbol-fonts.sh` block at `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` plus DejaVu on hosts where that file exists.

## Nits
1. **`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:33`** (not touched by the merge): the usage line `$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))` dates from when `orca-ide` was the GUI. After a switch it resolves to the CLI package. The test then stops at line 68 with "no GUI bin from …'s desktop Exec ('')". It fails loudly, but the line should say `bin/orca-ide-app`.
2. **`orca.nix:200`:** "Extracted once, shared by orca and macKeybindings" leaves out `orcaCli`, which runs `${appimageContents}/…/cli/index.js`. `orca-cli-skills.sh:132` finds the skills manifest through that same reference.
3. **`orca.nix` installCheck comment (~lines 136-139):** the pinned trees rely on fixup's `patchShebangs`/`patchELF` happening to change nothing. `installCheckPhase` would catch a change, so this fails closed. Setting `dontPatchELF = true` would turn that luck into intent, and the "(today they change nothing)" caveat could go. The comment's line wrapping is also uneven.
4. **Test gap in the fonts check (case 3, `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:111-126`):** it runs the host's `fc-match`/`fc-list` in a child, so it proves what children see, not what Orca itself sees.
   - `lib/orca/orca-ide` has no dynamic fontconfig or freetype dependency, so Chromium uses its own built-in copy to read the host's `fonts.conf`.
   - **Failure scenario:** if that built-in copy can't parse something in a newer Arch `fonts.conf`, Orca's own "DejaVu Sans Mono" lookup breaks. Case 5's ">100 colours" check would still pass on fallback text, so nothing would fail.
   - The deleted `sandbox-fonts.sh` had the same limit, so this is not a regression.
5. **`tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:114-128` ("GUI lifetime"):** with no bwrap, this passes trivially. It only guards against a `--die-with-parent`-style layer coming back, and the reworded comment says as much. Fine as a regression guard.

## Security
- **Chromium sandbox:** case 5 proves it on the real launch path, and the check can tell the cases apart: `--no-sandbox` would give `shared-ns+no-seccomp`, and no renderers found gives `''`, so either fails.
- **Fail-open paths:**
  - **`AppRun`:** removing it disables the CLI's `--no-sandbox` path in `electron-sandbox-switch.js`, and installCheck asserts it is gone.
  - **Explicit opt-out:** the only other way in is `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX=1`, set only after an explicit `<binary> --no-sandbox serve`. That is a user opt-in that predates this branch, not something it introduced.
  - **No user namespaces:** if they are unavailable, a non-setuid `chrome-sandbox` makes Chromium abort rather than run unsandboxed, so it fails closed.
- **Environment leakage beyond (a):** only `FONTCONFIG_FILE`, which is intended and covered by case 3. I found nothing else.
- **Test isolation:** `env -i` with an allowlist, a private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and D-Bus, a throwaway HOME (which also covers `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`DATA_HOME` defaults) and its own `--user-data-dir`. Nothing reaches the live `~/.orca`, `~/.config/orca`, `~/.claude` or keyring. The trap stops both units before `rm -rf "$T"`, `$T` comes from `mktemp` under `~/.cache` and is set before the trap is installed, and `RuntimeMaxSec` bounds any unit left by a SIGKILL.

## Regression coverage
- **Caught by a failing test or build:**
  - Re-sandboxing: cases 1 and 3.
  - Lost exec chain: case 5 pid check and case 6.
  - `--no-sandbox` creeping in: case 5, and installCheck for `AppRun`/`Exec`.
  - Pinned-tree drift: installCheck.
  - Ozone argv: the CLI test.
  - Missing dlopen RUNPATH: case 4.
- **Not caught:** the font-ranking drift in Important #1, and a failure in Orca's own built-in font lookup (nit 4).</result>

  # on fontconfig 2.18 by genericfamily, which no family-order rule in conf.d

  # monthly release (cache.nixos.org has only the default build: a 27 MB

====
#     installed -- a font it yields to but nothing installs is a hole, tofu

#

set -u
set -o pipefail

FLAKE="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"
[ -f "$FLAKE/flake.nix" ] || { echo "no flake.nix in: $FLAKE" >&2; exit 1; }
...
  # to, nothing from the host, over nixpkgs' conf.d.
  # Realised by drv, but only the default outputs are used: google-fonts also
  # has an adobeBlank output -- blank glyphs for every codepoint -- which the
  # profile never links and which would otherwise win every fallback.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  nix-store --realise $(jq -r '.yieldTo[]' <<<"$info") >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { fail "$h: fallback" "could not realise the fonts it yields to"; continue; }
  dirs=$(jq -r '.yieldToOut[]' <<<"$info")
  fc=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$h.pkgs.fontconfig.out" 2>/dev/null) \
    || { fail "$h: fallback" "could not realise fontconfig"; continue; }
  T=$(mktemp -d)
  {
    echo '<?xml version="1.0"?>'
    echo '<!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">'
    echo "<fontconfig><include ignore_missing=\"no\">$fc/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>"
    for d in $out $dirs; do echo "<dir>$d/share/fonts</dir>"; done
    echo "<cachedir>$T/cache</cachedir></fontconfig>"
  } > "$T/fonts.conf"
  for req in "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font" "NotoSans Nerd Font"; do
    for want in "23f5=Noto Sans Symbols 2" "1fb00=Noto Sans Symbols 2" \
                "23f8=Noto Color Emoji" "1f5a5=Noto Color Emoji" "2b50=Noto Color Emoji" \
                "2400!Noto Sans Symbols 2"; do
      case $want in
        *=*) cp=${want%%=*}; fam=${want#*=}; neg= ;;
        *) cp=${want%%!*}; fam=${want#*!}; neg=1 ;;
      esac
      got=$(XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$T/none" FONTCONFIG_FILE="$T/fonts.conf" \
        fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' "$req:charset=$cp" 2>/dev/null)
      if [ -z "$neg" ] && [ "$got" = "$fam" ]; then
        pass "$h: $req, U+$cp $(glyph $cp) -> $fam"
      elif [ -n "$neg" ] && [ -n "$got" ] && [ "$got" != "$fam" ]; then
        pass "$h: $req, U+$cp $(glyph $cp) -> $got, not $fam"
      elif [ -z "$neg" ]; then
        fail "$h: $req, U+$cp $(glyph $cp)" "falls back to '$got', want '$fam'"
      else
        fail "$h: $req, U+$cp $(glyph $cp)" "falls back to '$got', which it must not"
      fi
    done

content.text:
Review round 4's findings are all fixed, and round 5 is running on the new HEAD (0af5df11). No round has come back clean yet, so the two-in-a-row count is still at zero.

What changed in round 4:
- **Test can no longer touch your desktop:** every node-mode run of the GUI now has no display variables and an empty runtime dir. If node mode ever broke, the run would fail instead of opening a window.
- **The `serve` test uses the real CLI:** it now runs through the profile's `orca-cli` and prints which one ran. Before, it could silently fall back to running the CLI script directly.
- **Symbol gap font checked under Orca's font config:** DejaVu keeps all 143 (Mono) and 476 (Sans) glyphs it shares with `home.nix`'s gap font, so nothing changes face inside Orca. Comments carried over in the merge that still described the old sandboxed font setup are fixed.
- **Stray file removed:** a reviewer wrote `/dev/shm/x` (a codepoint list) against instructions. I checked it and deleted it.

The test suite passes 25/25.

Still waiting on you: keep, drop, or strip the nixGL variables that reach Orca's terminals.

Master hasn't moved, so the CLI branch is still merged in here directly rather than through master.

<result>I found no Critical findings and two Important ones. Both test suites pass. HEAD is 0af5df11 and `git status` is clean.

**Builds and runs**
- The requested eval returns `/nix/store/sbrpdvarvn22fwswm18kwlf74xvb4d1c-orca-1.4.238` and `/nix/store/1gvmjwxrihml84bbd5dfksr6ffcp6d66-orca-cli-1.4.238`. Both were already built.
- `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh`: 25/25 passed (via the systemd-run path, because this shell is a bwrap-era Orca terminal with no `/etc/hostname`). Renderers ran in their own user namespace with seccomp, a window mapped, the launched pid was Electron's, SIGTERM gave exit 0, and serve had `before=7` processes and `after=0`.
- `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`: 25/25 passed.
- Another session ran the GUI test at the same time as mine (unit `orca-gui-test-1083076`). Its leftover `~/.cache/orca-gui-test.*` and its document-portal FUSE mount were gone within about 90s. My own run cleaned up.

**What holds up**
- **Chromium sandbox:** fails closed. With no setuid bit and no user namespaces, Chromium aborts rather than running unsandboxed.
- **Ways to `--no-sandbox`:**
  - The CLI's AppRun check (`electron-sandbox-switch.js`) looks beside `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE`, or beside the raw binary when run in node mode. AppRun is removed, and installCheckPhase asserts that.
  - The `pft` path that appends `--no-sandbox` only applies to the AppImage-runtime daemon (it needs `APPDIR`), and there it is a node-script argument, not a Chromium switch.
  - The `ORCA_ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX` path only applies when the user passes `--no-sandbox` themselves.
- **Lost node mode is safe:** Orca's display gate runs before `requestSingleInstanceLock`, and it fails when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is unset. So a node-mode probe that lost `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` exits 1 before it could contact a live Orca. This also covers `orca-cli-skills.sh`'s `nodisplay`, which keeps the live runtime dir.
- **Test isolation:** confirmed. The keyring and document portal that D-Bus starts run under the private `$run` and the throwaway HOME (seen in the journal: `couldn't access control socket: …/run/keyring/control`). Orca's writes to `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.orca` went to `$T/home`.
- **Install-check gates:** these fail closed: `sha256sum -c --strict` on empty input, the `diff -r` and `lsx` diffs, and the Exec equality check.
- **RUNPATH order:** `patchELF` (shrink-rpath) runs before the manual `autoPatchelf` in postFixup, so the runtimeDependencies dirs survive. The dlopen case confirms it.

**Important**

1. **Case 6's readiness wait never fires** (`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:333`).
   - Every `orca-gui-test-*-serve.service` in the journal took 1min 30.3–31.6s, across 8 runs. That is the full `seq 90` loop plus about 1s of teardown. A loop that matched would finish in seconds.
   - In this build, `Terminal daemon:` is only printed inside the ready block when `e.health` is present (`wEt` in app.asar). The unconditional marker is `Orca server ready`.
   - Effect: every run spends 90s waiting, and the CLI is killed at an arbitrary point, maybe mid-startup. So the test does not prove that a *serving* server goes down.
   - If startup ever takes more than 90s, or the serve process dies, the case proceeds silently. It fails only if no Electron process exists at all.
   - Fix: wait for `Orca server ready` and fail the case if it never appears.
   - Regression coverage: the signal-forwarding check itself does still catch a non-exec wrapper.

2. **The fontconfig "takes nothing away" claim is false for language, math and per-character fallback** (`orca.nix:186-190`, `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:105-108`).
   - I compared the host's default config with `orca-fonts.conf` on the host (via `systemd-run`).
   - Same result for: serif, Helvetica, Times New Roman, Courier New, Verdana, emoji, cursive and ui-monospace.
   - Different results:
     - `:lang=ar`: Noto Nastaliq Urdu on the host, DejaVu Sans under Orca.
     - `:lang=he`: Open Sans on the host, DejaVu Sans under Orca.
     - `math`: Noto Sans Math on the host, DejaVu Math TeX Gyre under Orca.
   - Scenario: a browser or editor launched from an Orca terminal renders Hebrew or Arabic in DejaVu Sans, not the host's font. Orca's own Chromium fallback does the same.
   - Case 3 only checks five generic patterns, so it would not fail on this. Either reword the comment and test header ("adds DejaVu, which wins some language and per-character fallback"), or add `:lang=` and `math` probes and decide whether it matters.

**Nits**

- `orca.nix:86` is stale: "The AppImage ships bin/orca". The extracted AppImage has no `bin/`; `bin/orca` was what wrapType2 produced (the line was carried over from orca-cli-node:45). It should say it ships `orca-ide` at the root, plus AppRun.
- `orca.nix:146`: "no --no-sandbox carried over from upstream's line" suggests upstream's Exec has one. It is `Exec=AppRun %U`; AppRun adds the flag at runtime. Say "guarding against" instead.
- `orca.nix:23` says this is packaged "the way nixpkgs packages slack or vscode", but there is no `wrapGAppsHook3`. GSettings schemas come from the host's XDG_DATA_DIRS. That works on shiori because pacman's gtk3 owns `org.gtk.Settings.FileChooser.gschema.xml`. A GUI host without gtk3 would abort on the GTK file chooser with "No GSettings schemas", and no test opens a dialog.
- `orca.nix:127-131` and `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:306-307` say a signal to the CLI takes the server down. True for TERM, INT and HUP, but SIGKILL to the CLI (OOM, `timeout -s KILL`) still orphans Electron, since nothing sets a parent-death signal. Say "a catchable signal".
- **Shared `/tmp`:** Orca's daemon uses a fixed `/tmp/.orca-daemon-<uid>/terminals/<pid>.json` ledger. The live one exists (`27357.json`). Both test units share `/tmp`, so a test daemon can add entries to the live host-wide terminal ledger, and leave stale ones if SIGKILLed. This contradicts "never touches a running Orca". `--property=PrivateTmp=yes` on both systemd-run units would close it.
- **Live session D-Bus:** `appnode` (line 83) and `in_session` (line 235) keep the live `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`. This is harmless for node mode and grim, but the GTK clipboard helper (`--probe`, line 282) connects to the live bus. `-u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` in both costs nothing. HOME has to stay real for the font comparisons.
- **Concurrent runs:** the coredump check (line 352) filters by `$APP`, which is shared, so a crash in a concurrent run of the same build would be blamed on this one. This review saw concurrent runs happen.
- `ORCA_CLI` (line 314) is not in the test's usage header.
- `orca.nix:39` (82 columns) and `orca.nix:138` are over-long comment lines left from edits; the rest of the comment block wraps at 80.
- `orca-cli-skills.sh`'s GUI-lifetime case is now close to vacuous: with a plain exec nothing can kill the child. It only guards against a parent-death mechanism coming back. That is fine, but worth knowing.

**Would tests fail on regression?**

| Regression | Caught? | By |
|---|---|---|
| AppRun restored, or Exec changed or given `--no-sandbox` | Yes | build fails in installCheckPhase |
| `--no-sandbox` via the wrapper | Yes | case 5 (`shared-ns` / `no-seccomp`) |
| Pinned trees or manifest altered | Yes | installCheckPhase |
| Wrapper stops exec'ing | Yes | case 5 pid check and case 6 |
| Node mode broken | Yes | case 2 and the skills test |
| DejaVu missing | Yes | case 3 |
| Lang/math font divergence | No | — |
| Serve readiness | No | gate is dead code |
| Missing gsettings schemas | No | — |

The stale-comment grep turned up nothing else: the remaining bwrap and sandbox mentions describe the old setup or are unrelated.</result>

2. **"Adds DejaVu, takes nothing away" is false.** DejaVu Sans now wins Arabic, Hebrew and math fallback over your host fonts, inside Orca and in everything it spawns.

- **Chromium sandbox:** it can't silently fall back to unsandboxed. Without user namespaces, the non-setuid `chrome-sandbox` makes Chromium abort rather than run without a sandbox. For the profile CLI that executable is the nixGL wrapper's `bin/orca-ide-app`. `AppRun` only matters for the `process.execPath` fallback, i.e. the raw binary from item (b), so removing it is still correct. The main bundle's AppImage path that adds `--no-sandbox` needs `APPDIR`, which nothing sets.
- **Regression coverage:**

    - wrong fontconfig: case 3

1. **`tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:104-105` and `:120` (pre-existing on master): the node-mode probes are not kept off the desktop.** `nodisplay` unsets only `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_SOCKET` and `DISPLAY`. The real `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and `HOME` stay, and there is no `--user-data-dir`.
   - **Failure scenario:** a regression drops node mode (say the wrapper or nixGL starts clearing `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`). The "node mode" probe then launches a real GUI against the live `~/.config/orca` profile, live D-Bus and keyring, and `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wayland-0`. Today the live socket is `wayland-1`, so it would probably exit, but its single-instance lock can hand `-p "node-ok"` to the running Orca first.
   - **Fix:** the new test's `appnode` (`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:88-90`) already does this right, with an empty private runtime dir and D-Bus unset. The cli-skills test should match it.

3. **`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:248-251`, `:359`:** nothing checks that `PrivateTmp` actually took effect, e.g. by asserting the unit's `/tmp` has no `.orca-daemon-$UID`. systemd fails the unit rather than ignoring the setting, so this is unproven rather than fail-open.

**State:** HEAD is b1120d2c and `git status` is clean (`.drovr/` and `.entire/` are ignored). `origin/master` was f6f90d3e both before and after `git fetch`, the same as the merge-base. The eval gives `orca-1.4.238` = `/nix/store/w7w62kzkf2x4211mywzyda5b383rlxn7-orca-1.4.238` (the nixGL layer over `l98blyx4…-orca-1.4.238`) and `orca-cli-1.4.238` = `/nix/store/REDACTED.4.238`.

**Test runs:**
- `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh`: 34/34 passed in 40s. Case 6 counted 7 server processes before the signal and 0 after.
- `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`: 25/25 passed.
- `tests/symbol-fonts.sh`: 53/53 passed.

My shell runs inside a sandbox with no `/etc/hostname`, so the new test took its `systemd-run --user` branch.

**Checks that held up:**
- The generated wrapper is `bash -e`. It exports `FONTCONFIG_FILE`, applies the ozone rule (`[ -n "$explicit" ] || [ -n "${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ] || set -- …`, which is safe under `-e`), then does a plain `exec "…/lib/orca/orca-ide" "$@"`.
- The ozone rule matches Orca's own check (`PEN` in app.asar). It also matches Electron's run-as-node test, which treats an empty `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` as unset.
- The desktop file reads `Exec=orca-ide-app %U`, keeps `x-scheme-handler/orca;`, and `StartupWMClass=orca` matches the window's app_id.
- In installCheckPhase, every manifest key shape is covered (`commonSha256`, `targets.*.files`). The `ripgrep/*` fallback resolves correctly, and the linux-x64-glibc `.runtime-node` pin matches `node-runtime/bin/node`. stdenv's `pipefail` plus `sha256sum -c` fails loudly on an empty or partial list.
- Relative `conf.d` in the host's fonts.conf resolves to `/etc/fonts/conf.d` (seen with `FC_DEBUG`).
- `agent-browser-linux-x64` still runs after patching (`--version` prints 0.27.0).

## Critical
None.

## Important
1. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:54 — failed transient units pile up on the live user manager.** In the sandbox branch, `host()` calls `systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --quiet` without `--collect`. Any probe that exits non-zero leaves a `run-p…service` in the failed state. Three such calls fail on every passing run:
   - `coredumpctl list` at :370 exits 1 when there are no dumps.
   - The `systemctl --user stop … "$unit-serve"` in the trap at :81 targets units that are already gone.
   - `reset-failed` at :316 targets a unit that `--collect` already removed.

   `systemctl --user list-units --failed` on this machine now shows 26 of these units (9 coredumpctl, 9 stop, 8 reset-failed) from runs of this script. That clutters the live session's failed-unit state, which breaks "tests must never touch the live desktop". The fix is to add `--collect` to `host()`. The test still fails on regression; this is cleanup only.

## Nits
1. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:128-144 — font cases measure the host's fontconfig, not Electron's.** The children's view is checked with Arch's `/usr/bin/fc-match`/`fc-list`. `lib/orca/orca-ide` does not link `libfontconfig`; it carries its own copy built in. So "'DejaVu Sans Mono' exists for the app" proves what children see, not what the app's own text rendering resolves. A regression that only Electron's built-in fontconfig hits (a parse or version difference) would pass. Case 5's render check would not catch it either (see nit 2).
2. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:281-291 — "it renders a UI" is weak.** It sleeps 10s and then requires more than 100 colours. An error page, a crash dialog, or a UI in the wrong font (the original Montserrat Thin bug) also has hundreds of antialiased colours, and the fixed sleep could flake on a slow first frame.
3. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:135-140 and orca.nix (fontsConf comment) — the ":lang= fallback stays with the host" result depends on the host's fonts.** In my sandboxed shell, which can't see the Noto Arabic faces, the app's fontconfig sends `:lang=ar` and `:lang=ka` to DejaVu Sans Mono, while plain host fontconfig gives Rubik and Noto Sans. On shiori's full font set the test passes. So the comment's "Sans Mono alone leaves all of those to the host" holds per host, not in general, and a pass on shiori says nothing about utsuho.
4. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:351-356 — case 6 cannot tell a TERM-driven shutdown from a server that died on its own** between the `before` count and the kill. Only SIGTERM is exercised; INT and HUP, which orca.nix's comment names, are not.
5. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:370 — the coredump check can pass without checking anything.** If `coredumpctl` is missing or denied, `2>/dev/null || true` gives empty output and the case passes.
6. **tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:253 — `TZ="${TZ:-}"` turns an unset TZ into an empty one,** which glibc reads as UTC inside the case 5 session. This is harmless today because no case 5 assertion uses the time zone.
7. **orca.nix (installPhase AppRun comment and the `[ ! -e $out/lib/orca/AppRun ]` check) — the stated reason doesn't match what the CLI checks.** The CLI's `needsElectronNoSandbox` looks for AppRun next to `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE`, which is `$orcaGui/bin/orca-ide-app`, so it searches `bin/`, never `lib/orca`. Removing AppRun only matters for launches of the raw `lib/orca/orca-ide`. The removal is still right; the comment overstates what it protects. Separately, no case checks that renderers stay sandboxed for GUIs started by the CLI (`open`/`serve`); case 5 only checks a desktop-file launch.
8. **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:118-131 — the "GUI lifetime" case now only guards against a re-added die-with-parent.** Nothing in the new design could kill the child, so it passes almost by construction. The comment says as much; just noting it is a regression guard only.

## Would the tests fail on regression?
Yes, for each part of the intent:
- **bwrap back:** cases 1 and 3 (hostname, localtime) and case 6.
- **Wrapper stops exec'ing:** the case 5 pid check.
- **Ozone flag injected in node mode:** case 2 and the cli-skills node-mode case.
- **Explicit-platform handling lost:** the cli-skills argv cases.
- **FONTCONFIG_FILE wrong, or all of DejaVu added back:** the case 3 font cases.
- **ANGLE/SwiftShader rpath or runtimeDependencies missing:** the case 4 dlopen check.
- **Pinned trees changed, AppRun back, or desktop Exec altered:** the build itself fails in installCheckPhase.

The gaps are Electron's built-in font resolution (nit 1), how strict the render check is (nit 2), and the coredump check (nit 5).</result>

A `--no-sandbox` renderer would be readable, so a real false pass is unlikely. Still, it should require both namespace IDs to be non-empty.

Round 7 had one Important finding, the GTK one; I've fixed it, committed (a4fc8c95), and round 8 is running on that commit. No round has come back clean yet, so the two-clean-rounds count is still 0.

- **GTK file dialogs:** I left out nixpkgs' usual GTK wrapper (`wrapGAppsHook3`) on purpose: it would push `XDG_DATA_DIRS` and similar variables into every process Orca starts. Instead, the test now checks that the app's GTK can read your host's file-chooser settings schema. The comment in `orca.nix` explains the trade-off.
- **New test checks:**
  - nixGL is actually in the launch path; the headless render check would never notice it missing.
  - The test session really gets its own `/tmp`.
  - The renderer sandbox check only counts processes whose namespaces it could actually read.
- **Cleanup:**
  - `libappindicator-gtk3` is gone; nothing in the binary loads it.
  - The test's exit cleanup now handles read-only files Orca copies into the throwaway home.
  - A few labels and comments are reworded.
